decisive_items: Revealed raised liver enzyme levels and positive anti–hepatitis C virus antibody status
lichenoid plaques on the right angle of mouth, bilateral buccal mucosa, and erosions covered with hemorrhagic crusts on the upper and lower lips
Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis
response.rationale: R2 uniquely integrates the positive anti-HCV serology with the clinical and histopathological features of lichen planus, providing the most complete and clinically actionable diagnosis. C1 captures the mucocutaneous distribution but omits the HCV association, which is a key etiological factor.

rejected.why: General lichen planus without specifying the HCV association or the mucocutaneous extent.
Nail-only focus misses the oral mucosal involvement and HCV association.
Accurate for mucocutaneous LP but fails to incorporate the positive HCV serology.
Overly narrow (nail-only, erosive) and ignores oral and HCV findings.
